item.research_question: How can ultrahigh-Ni, cobalt-free single-crystalline cathodes be stabilized against chemomechanical degradation, thermal instability, and oxygen loss to enable commercial high-energy lithium-ion batteries?
item.processing_route: In situ high-entropy doping during hydroxide coprecipitation followed by lithiation at a raised sintering temperature to produce single-crystalline particles with 3 to 4 μm size
item.test_conditions: Half and full pouch cells cycled between 2.8 and 4.3 V (up to 3500 cycles) and 2.8 to 4.5 V (up to 1000 cycles) at 25°C and 55°C; thermal abuse tests from 25 to 500°C; in situ XRD and DEMS during charging and heating
key_findings: HE-SC-N88 achieved 92.4% capacity retention after 2500 cycles and 80.6% after 3500 cycles at 2.8–4.3 V (25°C), with a capacity loss of only 0.0055% per cycle.
At 55°C, HE-SC-N88 retained 91.5% capacity after 1000 cycles (2.8–4.3 V), losing only 0.0085% per cycle.
HE-SC-N88 maintained 81.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 4.6 V, compared to 56.9% for SC-NCM88.
The H2-H3 phase transition peak shift was reduced from 1.16° in SC-NCM88 to 0.63° in HE-SC-N88, with lattice volume contraction reduced from -8.06% to -4.20%.
Thermal exothermic peak temperature for oxygen evolution increased from 200.3°C (SC-NCM88) to 243.7°C (HE-SC-N88), with total heat release dropping from 846.5 J g−1 to 327.8 J g−1.
Phase transitions upon heating were delayed: layered-to-spinel at 213°C (vs. 156°C), spinel-to-M3O4 at 296°C (vs. 238°C), and M3O4-to-rock-salt at 352°C (vs. 256°C).
No intragranular cracks were observed in HE-SC-N88 during heating to 500°C, whereas SC-NCM88 developed cracks by 300°C.
CEI layer thickness on cycled HE-SC-N88 was ultrathin (<3 nm rock-salt surface layer), while SC-NCM88 developed CEI >20 nm with extensive rock-salt and spinel phases.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute stability to a synergistic effect: Mg2+ ions occupy Li sites acting as pillars to inhibit slab sliding and TM ion migration; high-valent dopants (Ti4+, Nb5+, Mo6+) strengthen TM-O bonds; the high-entropy configuration induces an 'entropy-stabilization' effect that reduces lattice strain; and the single-crystalline morphology eliminates grain boundaries, preventing intergranular crack propagation.
item.limitations: The text notes that operating at 4.7 V is limited by the 'innate intolerance to high potentials of organic electrolyte itself' and that some capacity reduction is typical when introducing heteroatoms, though minimized here.
item.future_work: The authors propose that this collaborative strategy provides guidance for developing advanced Co-free cathodes for next-generation LIBs and other rechargeable battery systems.
quotes: HE-SC-N88 is featured with a grain-boundary-free and stabilized structure with minimal lattice strain, preventing mechanical degradation, reducing surface parasitic reactions, and mitigating oxygen loss.

The synergistic effect of the HE framework and SC design in HE-SC-N88 establishes an ultrastable lattice that resisted chemomechanical breakdown even during prolonged cycling across a broad voltage range (4.3 to 4.7 V versus Li/Li+).

item.research_question: How does high-entropy doping (using Mg, Fe, Ti, Nb, Mo) in a Co-free single-crystalline Ni-rich cathode affect its synthesis, structural stability, thermal safety, and electrochemical performance compared to conventional Co-containing and non-doped counterparts?
item.material_system: Ni0.88Mn0.03Mg0.02Fe0.02Ti0.02Mo0.02Nb0.01(OH)2 precursors for HE-SC-N88 and HE-PC-N88; Ni0.88Co0.09Mn0.03(OH)2 for SC-NCM88 and PC-NCM88; final cathodes: SC-NCM88, HE-SC-N88, PC-NCM88, HE-PC-N88
item.processing_route: Coprecipitation in a 30 L bath-type tank reactor at 55°C, pH 11.0–11.5, 600 rpm stirring, with synchronous feeding of 6 mol L⁻¹ NaOH and 0.7 mol L⁻¹ NH4OH; sintering at 550°C for 6 h and 820°C for 15 h under O2 flow (0.8 L min⁻¹) for single crystals; 750°C for 12 h for polycrystals; particle sizes 3–4 μm (SC) or 12–14 μm (PC)
item.test_conditions: Half cells: 2032-type coin cells, Li metal counter, 1.0 mol L⁻¹ LiPF6 in EC/EMC/DEC (1/1/1) + 5 wt% FEC, 25°C or 55°C, cutoff voltages 4.3–4.7 V vs Li/Li⁺, 1 C = 200 mA g⁻¹; Thermal: DEMS (charged to 4.5 V, 0.2 C), DSC (30–450°C, 10°C min⁻¹), TR-XRD (25–600°C, 4°C min⁻¹), in situ heating TEM (21–500°C, 10°C min⁻¹); Full cells: 5.1 Ah, 2.8–4.3/4.5 V, 0.1 C activation
key_findings: HE-type precursors were successfully synthesized with a selective stoichiometric ratio of Ni0.88Mn0.03Mg0.02Fe0.02Ti0.02Mo0.02Nb0.01(OH)2 via coprecipitation.
Single-crystalline HE-SC-N88 particles achieved a median size of 3 to 4 μm, while polycrystalline HE-PC-N88 reached 12 to 14 μm.
Thermal stability was evaluated using DEMS, DSC, TR-XRD, and in/ex situ heating TEM on delithiated cathodes charged to 4.5 V or 4.7 V.
In situ XRD measurements were recorded with an interval of 20 min for each 2θ scan from 10° to 80° during charging/discharging at 0.2 C.
Atomic-resolved STEM-HAADF images were captured in adequately thin regions of the particles because the resolution was confined by the thickness of the cathodes.
The capacity balance of anode to cathode in full cells was about 1.14 with loading masses of 30.0 mg cm⁻² (cathode) and 21.8 mg cm⁻² (anode).
All cycled cathodes for post-mortem characterizations were in the discharged states and washed in DMC for 12 hours before testing.
The concentration of both O2 and H2O in the glove box used for cell fabrication was kept less than 0.1 ppm.
quotes: The HE-type precursor with a selective stoichiometric ratio of Ni0.88Mn0.03Mg0.02Fe0.02-Ti0.02Mo0.02Nb0.01(OH)2 is synthesized for HE-SC-N88.
During the coprecipitation process, the pH value was accurately kept between 11.0 and 11.5, and the reaction temperature was constantly retained at 55°C.

The thermal decomposition of the delithiated cathodes during in situ heating TEM test was investigated in real time by heating the charged cathodes ranging from 21° to 500°C at a heating rate of 10°C min⁻¹.
